messages.subject: Same initialisation values
parts:
Hi everyone,
 
I have something to clarify but think this might be a stupid question XD. If I run 2 chains and have the same initialisation values for both chains, and the traceplot of the parameters show a great mixing which means it converges very well. Is this somewhat like "cheating" because I use the same initialisation values for both the chains? Thank you for those who answer my question! :)) Part of the code is as follows:
 
 
inits <- list("alpha"=0.4,"pi1"=0.2,"tau"=c(0.24,0.65,0.93,1.2,1.6,2.3,7.6,12.5),"u"=runif(length(y)))
inits <- rep(list(inits),2)
c_dat= list(J=9,I=length(y),y=y)
fit<- stan(model_code=c_code,data=c_dat,iter=1000,chains=2,warmup=100,inits=inits)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Same initialisation values
parts:
That depends on who you ask :-)

We like to recommend that you start with more diffuse
initial points to make sure that the initial points have
been "forgotten". Otherwise, you might think you've converged
when you haven't.

Others might recommend you just run one chain for a very very
very very very very long time. The point is that asymptotically
the result's the same :-)

Having said that, you often need to initialize with a single
reasonable value just for convenience.

In the future, we want to add a controllable bit of randomization
around a user-specified initialization point. The problem with
doing this yourself is that you need to respect the constraints.
We can just work on the unconstrained scale internally the way we
do for default inits.

- Bob
